simple.meaning: תְּלָת (tᵉlâth) is a Hebrew object word meaning “three or third.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Ezra 6:4. The surrounding context includes kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to תְּלָת (H8532) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: תְּלָת (tᵉlâth) / H8532 is traced through Ezra 6:4, Ezra 6:15, Daniel 3:23, Daniel 3:24 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: with three courses of great stones and a course of new timber. Let the expenses be given out of the king’s house.

timeline.evidenceText: with three courses of great stones and a course of new timber. Let the expenses be given out of the king’s house.
This house was finished on the third day of the month Adar, which was in the sixth year of the reign of Darius the king.
These three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, fell down bound into the middle of the burning fiery furnace.
Then Nebuchadnezzar the king was astonished, and rose up in haste. He spoke and said to his counselors, “Didn’t we cast three men bound into the middle of the fire?”
Then this Daniel was distinguished above the presidents and the local governors, because an excellent spirit was in him; and the king thought to set him over the whole realm.
Then these men assembled together, and found Daniel making petition and supplication before his God.
Then the king, when he heard these words, was very displeased, and set his heart on Daniel to deliver him; and he labored until the going down of the sun to rescue him.
“Behold, there was another animal, a second, like a bear. It was raised up on one side, and three ribs were in its mouth between its teeth. They said this to it: ‘Arise! Devour much flesh!’

“I considered the horns, and behold, there came up among them another horn, a little one, before which three of the first horns were plucked up by the roots: and behold, in this horn were eyes like the eyes of a man, and a mouth speaking great things.

and concerning the ten horns that were on its head, and the other horn which came up, and before which three fell, even that horn that had eyes, and a mouth that spoke great things, whose look was more stout than its fellows.
As for the ten horns, ten kings will arise out of this kingdom. Another will arise after them; and he will be different from the former, and he will put down three kings.
